summary: Courtney Bruntz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015) and later held posts at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, Craig Jamieson served at the University of Cambridge (attested 2002), where he was attested in 2012 as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection. He also became a fellow of Queens' College, Cambridge.
Craig Preston is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and with Jeffrey Hopkins from 1980 to 1981.

Cristina Pecchia specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Sapienza University of Rome (~1999–2003) under Raniero Gnoli, Raffaele Torella, and Corrado Pensa, also studying under Ernst Steinkellner at the University of Vienna in 2000.

Csaba Dezső is an Indologist who earned master's degrees at Eötvös Loránd University (~1991–1997) and a PhD from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1998–2004). He served as an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University (~2003).

Csaba Kiss works in Indology and religious studies. He earned a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2024) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. Her academic appointments include Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and a post at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi and a PhD under John R. McRae at Indiana University Bloomington, later serving as an adjunct lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel works in history and archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2009).
Cynthia Col studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman. Her work encompasses sinology, religious studies, and Tibetology.
Cynthia M. Beall is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her studies at Pennsylvania State University (~1970–1976) and joined the faculty of Case Western Reserve University in 1976.
Cynthia Talbot is an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1980–1988) and became a professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Cyril Henry Philips was a historian and Indologist educated at the University of Liverpool (1931–1934) and SOAS (~1936–1940). He served as director of SOAS from 1957, succeeding Ralph Lilley Turner, and as vice-chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).

Cyrus Stearns is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Washington (-1996) under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, also studying with Turrell V. Wylie. He has served as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cécile Ducher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Matthew T. Kapstein (-2017), where she also served as a research fellow.

D. C. Lau was a scholar of sinology and philosophy who studied at the University of Hong Kong and the University of Glasgow. He held appointments at SOAS, the University of London, UCL, and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1978–1989).
D. C. Sarasvati was an Indology scholar who studied under V. Raghavan. Sarasvati served as a lecturer-cum-research assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.
D. L. Narasimhachar was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1927–1932). He served on the faculty at the University of Mysore from ~1932 to 1962.
